name: Ulusalism
summary: Ulusalism (ulusalcılık) is a Turkish secularist neo-nationalism descended from Kemalism, which took a left-nationalist form from the 1990s under figures like Attila İlhan, Mümtaz Soysal and Doğu Perinçek. It defends the unitary, ethnically homogeneous republic, the army and strict secularism, opposes Islamism, the EU, the US and globalism, and sees foreign plots to partition Turkey. Its economics is state-led and production-focused, and it looks to Russia and China as a counterweight to the West.
scope: The 1990s-onward left-nationalist current as represented by Perinçek's Patriotic (Vatan) Party and the Kemalist-Eurasianist milieu, drawn from secondary descriptions and party declarations reported in the press. It excludes older uses of 'ulusalcılık' as a mere synonym for nationalism and the mainstream CHP. Economic and social-policy answers are mostly low-confidence inferences, as the sources document foreign policy, secularism and state structure far better.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Self-described left-wing nationalists favour a provider state, but the sources document no health policy; inferred from the left label.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the movement's left-wing self-description and production-and-labour framing; no wage position is documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Perinçek blames Turkey's post-1980 integration into the world economy for cutting it off from production, implying distrust of free markets; stated only indirectly.

public-ownership.rationale: The party's production revolution and plan to turn private schools public point toward state ownership of strategic sectors; inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing label; the sources give no tax programme.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the left-nationalist self-image; unions are not discussed in the sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: A statist production programme with rent ceilings suggests property yields to national needs; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Rent monitoring boards and state-led production imply support for regulation; inferred, not directly stated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Left-wing nationalists are unlikely to favour cutting welfare, but the sources never discuss it.

worker-ownership.rationale: The movement puts the nation above class, so workers' ownership is not a goal; inferred from its nationalist emphasis.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The party makes ending terrorism a first priority, so security measures are likely accepted; surveillance itself is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Wikipedia notes socially conservative positions among many adherents; drugs are not specifically discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents back laws protecting Turkishness yet defend free speech against Islamist rule; sources are silent, so split.

strong-leader.rationale: Kemalist tradition prizes a strong republican state, but ulusalcı opposition to Erdoğan cuts the other way; weakly positive inference.

state-harmful.rationale: The party's declaration centres the security and unity of the nation and state, the opposite of anti-statism.

limit-guns.rationale: Order-minded Kemalist statism implies tight gun control; not documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: The army is the movement's main base and the party wants a national military-industrial complex independent of the West.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socially conservative leanings among adherents suggest opposition; not documented.

decide-locally.rationale: The National State Declaration stresses the unity of the Republic and the integrity of its territory, favouring centralised authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Tough line on terrorism versus no stated penal philosophy; sources give no basis to lean either way.

traditional-family.rationale: Wikipedia reports many ulusalcılar take socially conservative positions on gender politics.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Perinçek rejects what he calls the imposition of homosexuality and a third gender and opposes its promotion.

abortion-legal.rationale: Secular Kemalists accept legal abortion while nationalists favour births; the sources are silent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Perinçek names enlightenment and secularism as one of Turkey's three big issues; the movement arose against AKP Islamism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: A nation-first, homogeneity-minded movement is unlikely to back group remedies; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Perinçek's rejection of a imposed third gender implies rejection of constructivist views of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Insistence on an ethnically homogeneous, secular nation and radicalised Kemalist historiography make cultural preservation central.

gradual-change.rationale: The declaration seeks to carry the Kemalist revolution to decisive victory, a revolutionary rather than gradualist idiom; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Substack analysis says the movement objects to migration given its view of a homogeneous nation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement opposes globalist influence and Western hegemony, so strengthening bodies like the UN runs against it.

free-trade.rationale: The party wants a production revolution and says integration into the world economy after 1980 severed production.

nation-first.rationale: Sustaining the nation-state and independence is the core of the movement; slogan is a totally independent Turkey.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents see Western powers as plotting against Turkey, so rights-based intervention would be read as a pretext; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A homogeneous-nation view and objection to migration exclude open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The party's programme is a production revolution aimed at growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No environmental position is documented and none can be inferred with confidence.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Kemalist positivism and a national military-industrial drive suggest technological optimism; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The party promises cheap domestic energy and independence; nuclear power is not mentioned.

revolution-justified.rationale: The party calls for carrying the Kemalist revolution to decisive victory; Perinçek's roots are Maoist.

experts-over-public.rationale: Kemalist guardianship traditions favour elite and bureaucratic expertise; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: A production revolution is state-led, but the sources describe no planned economy; split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Neither endorsed nor rejected in the sources.

land-value-tax.rationale: Taxing land value as a single tax belongs to Georgist thought; none of the opened sources links ulusalcılar to it, so this is a neutral placeholder.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Left-nationalists plausibly favour taxing large estates, but this is inferred from the left label alone and not a documented plank.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional state income does not appear in the party's production-focused declarations, and adherents give no sign of a view either way.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protecting national production from world-economy integration is the core of the party's economic message.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The party advocates a national military-industrial complex and a state-led production revolution.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Sources give no view on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A nationalist movement that keeps the nation-state cannot be aiming at a moneyless society; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A strong-state movement would not leave money to the market; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Putting the nation over class suggests solidarist arrangements; not documented.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ulusalcı groups compete as parties and oppose AKP dominance; inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Defending the Republic and the Kemalist revolution excludes hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents are republican but distrust voters who chose Islamist rule; sources do not settle it.

direct-votes.rationale: Kemalist elitism favours representation over plebiscites; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: A unitary-state nationalist party rejects council power; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial integrity and the unity of the Republic are the first items of the party's declaration.

natural-rulers.rationale: No stated position; Kemalist elitism leans one way, republican equality the other.

political-violence-never.rationale: Adherents are not pacifist given army and Maoist background; inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement's army ties and Blue Homeland doctrine suggest martial values; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secularism is central, but the Turkish model is state supervision of religion rather than strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement is secularist and formed against AKP Islamism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: It centres the state's security role; privatised defence is the opposite.

military-superiority.rationale: The party seeks a military-industrial complex independent of Western powers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Substack analysis says they hold the nation should be ethnically homogeneous and secular.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement subordinates class to nation; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The movement mixes a left label with nationalist class-collaboration, and no source says whether it seeks equal outcomes or only opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Unitary-state nationalism leaves little room for group land authority; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism and Third Worldism are keywords of the movement, implying sympathy.

civilizational-union.rationale: Their Eurasian bloc is geopolitical and secular, not religion-based; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Duty to nation is emphasised over self-interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Nation and state primacy suggests duty-first framing; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the sources; the movement's concerns are sovereignty and production, so there is no basis to lean.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalists tend to prize population strength; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The party calls for more production, not less.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources say nothing about disruptive technology, and a movement that prizes established national institutions has mixed incentives.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist questions are not addressed in any opened source on ulusalcılık, so neutrality is the honest answer.

algorithmic-government.rationale: State-centred nationalism would not hand rule to algorithms; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security-first posture suggests state access; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement frames itself as progressive Kemalist enlightenment rather than restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: A doctrinal Kemalist movement would put ideology first; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Parties and institutions are the vehicle; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source discusses the ethics of means versus ends for the movement; its history spans parliamentary parties and Maoist cadres.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Nationalist left keeps work-based distribution; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Emphasis on production is not framed as against profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Left self-label versus nationalist class collaboration; unresolved in sources.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship conflicts with nationalism over class; inferred.

collective-farming.rationale: Agriculture policy is not covered in the declarations I opened; collectivisation is not part of a Kemalist nationalist programme as documented.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialism is a keyword of the movement; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: A statist movement whose declarations centre the security and capacity of the state would reject the view that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Collective national concerns outweigh libertarian limits; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nation-centred ideology treats the national community as a rights-bearer and a priority, so it would reject an individuals-only view; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Army-centred movement; conscription not explicitly discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Ulusalcılar stress attachment to the homeland and its territorial integrity, which cuts against valuing exit above political voice; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers who may leave contradicts the state-and-nation-first outlook in the party's declaration.

positive-liberty.rationale: Left label suggests material conditions matter; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents blame foreign and liberal elites, but no source states a claim that universities and media outweigh elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not stated; Kemalist civic tradition leans against, but nationalists vary.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation through families and guilds is not documented for this movement, which works through parties like the Vatan Party.

total-state.rationale: Strong state but no documented totalising claim.

national-rebirth.rationale: The declaration seeks decisive victory for the Kemalist revolution against perceived threats; inferred rebirth framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Blue Homeland doctrine claims maritime space but is framed as defence.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Oath-bound feudal authority is far from the republican, Kemalist state that adherents defend.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom-like obligations contradict the republican modernism of the Kemalist revolution the movement wants to complete.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The movement's claim of enlightenment and its own historiography assume knowable truth rather than power-relative knowledge; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Enlightenment framing suggests universalist reason; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: National-interest politics assumes one national good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Israel is named among the states in the alleged conspiracy against Turkey, but the statement is not directly addressed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Sources are silent on diaspora return; Turkish nationalism could be sympathetic to kin abroad, but nothing documents a stance.

revive-national-language.rationale: Revival of a disused language is not an issue the sources tie to ulusalcılar; Turkish is already the state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Public or worker votes on corporate governance are not mentioned in the party's production-revolution declarations.

school-vouchers.rationale: Perinçek's programme would convert private schools into public schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The documented economic message is about production and rent policy, not fiscal rules, so there is no basis to lean.

economic-freedom.rationale: A state-led production programme and scepticism of world-market integration imply political freedom does not depend on economic freedom; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Reliance on rulers' moral example over law fits a Confucian outlook, not a legalistic republican movement like this one.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sustaining the nation-state and independence is central to the movement.

force-without-un.rationale: The Blue Homeland doctrine suggests willingness to act without outside approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Enlightenment and secularism are named as priorities.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare conditions are not discussed; the movement's welfare views are undocumented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Left nationalists subordinate class conflict to national unity and independence, so cooperation between employers and workers fits; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Contrary to its emphasis on preserving culture and historiography.

dominated-front.rationale: The party's programme proposes closer ties with Russia, China and a regional bloc as a counterweight to the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement is described as leftist discourse combined with nationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatism versus Kemalist women's equality; unresolved.

ban-interest.rationale: A secularist movement has no reason to adopt Islamic bans on interest, and the production-first programme does not propose one.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not documented; contrary to republican citizenship.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state as a ruling-class tool is not documented as an ulusalcı doctrine, despite Perinçek's Maoist past.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Cheap domestic energy for producers is promised.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The nation is seen as homogeneous and objection to migration is documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: The conspiracy-minded strand targets foreign plots against Turkey; replacement by immigration not documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral-system reform is not discussed in the sources, so adherents' preference is unknown.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wikipedia notes socially conservative gender positions, but no source shows adherents' view on structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-elite stance towards liberal Kemalist elite and AKP; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not documented; contrary to Kemalist modernism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement is army-aligned and opposed trials of officers; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Declarations demand state-led production, rent ceilings and public schools, which is far from a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No source reports a racial-mixing doctrine; Kemalist nationalism is cultural rather than racial in the available material.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Citizen equality is Kemalist, though homogeneity limits it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Nationalist left accepts national roads; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents name Israel among alleged plotters, but the sources do not give a view on settler colonialism as a concept.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Secularism implies one civil law for all citizens.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not discussed; secularism opposes religious regulation, while nationalists distrust missionaries, so it is split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle protection is a South Asian issue with no tie to Turkish nationalism or any opened source.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Enlightenment and secularism are named priorities.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Perception of hostile encirclement and strong state; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Kemalist doctrine that sovereignty belongs to the nation underlies the movement, so legitimacy through consent fits; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Production focus implies export orientation; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented; conspiratorial view of minorities complicates.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: An army-aligned, security-minded movement does not hold a pacifist libertarian principle of non-initiation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: No source frames struggle between peoples as the engine of progress for ulusalcılar, so neutrality.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Turkey has a long record of closing parties, and the movement's defence of the republic suggests support for bans; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-domination rhetoric on foreign powers; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Sources do not address checks and balances; adherents criticise AKP concentration of power but have no stated constitutional model.

vanguard-party.rationale: Perinçek's Maoist background suggests sympathy with disciplined cadre parties, but the present nationalist programme is not vanguardist; inferred negative.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left self-description implies concern for the poor, but the sources show no explicit priority; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British issue, and no source ties ulusalcılar to it; neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: A left-labelled movement would not favour restricting strikes, but labour law is not documented; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Neomalthusian explanations of poverty are not part of the documented outlook; the party blames Turkey's economic opening.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Insisting that the nation be ethnically homogeneous implies diversity is seen as a threat to cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition conflicts with a state-centred republican outlook that values trained institutions and the Kemalist elite tradition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Fear of encirclement and partition plots, plus army ties, makes emergency measures against internal enemies plausible; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Perinçek proposes rent freezes and ceilings to curb inflation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Adherents are themselves opposition journalists and parties, and no source supports ruling-party media control.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army is a guardian institution, not party-controlled; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A homogeneity-minded movement that objects to migration would favour a long wait for citizenship; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay caps for legislators are not documented as an ulusalcı demand.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not discussed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposition to Western hegemony and globalist influence.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive versus legislative command of the military is not addressed, and the movement criticises the presidential system only indirectly.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Episcopal church governance has no relevance to a Turkish secularist movement; neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by senior religious scholars is the opposite of the secularism the movement defends against Islamism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism contradicts a nationalist movement whose first aim is the nation's security and territorial integrity.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship is not documented as an ulusalcı position, and Kemalists claim an enlightenment mantle, so neutral.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Adherents oppose Erdoğan's long rule and the presidential system, so unlimited re-election is probably rejected; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not discussed in the sources.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Questioning of NATO membership is noted and Western domination is opposed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rent controls rather than abolition proposed.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry replacing the army contradicts the movement's army-centred, state-security outlook.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Anti-urban moralism is not part of the documented Kemalist nationalist outlook, so neutral.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The proposed bloc includes the TRNC; inferred sympathy for reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Adherents criticise liberal elites but also revere Enlightenment education, so no clear line emerges.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Seen as West in crisis, yet Kemalist civilizational ladder; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: A tough stance on terrorism, especially the PKK, makes capital punishment plausible, though no source states it; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Mixed Kemalist education with rejection of gender ideology promotion.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Perinçek names enlightenment and secularism as a core issue, which rules out religious teaching of creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Socially conservative leanings among adherents suggest support for restriction; not documented specifically.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Kemalist citizenship is traditionally civic, but homogeneity-minded nationalists may prefer descent; the sources do not settle it.

minority-language-support.rationale: A homogeneous nation and Kurdish concerns exclude minority language rights.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Secular uniform law is a Kemalist principle, so exemptions for minorities' religious practice would be disfavoured; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Millian celebration of eccentricity is at odds with socially conservative homogeneity, but no source addresses it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialism and Third Worldism are keywords of the movement, so sympathy for debt relief is plausible; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: No source reports the movement's view on rewriting the constitution through an assembly; it defends the Kemalist republic.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The sources give no stance on trading political freedoms for development; adherents split between nationalism and Kemalist authoritarian-modernisation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: A nation-first movement is unlikely to stress duties of aid to the world's poor; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Independence from West; nuclear not discussed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Adherents oppose Erdoğan's presidency, but there is no documented stance on how a head of state should be chosen.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial integrity of the homeland is the first declaration item.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: A production-first, rent-capping programme implies property is justified by service to the nation; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterisation of the USSR is not covered in the opened sources; Perinçek's Maoist past hints at one view, but it is unconfirmed.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not documented in these sources.

collective-defense.rationale: The movement questions NATO and Western domination, yet also fears encirclement and may value alliances, so it is split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources do not address unlawful annexation; the Cyprus question might cut either way for adherents.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Turkish secularism subordinates religion to the state; inferred from secularism.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Kemalist republicanism ascribes a unifying national role to the head of state; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents see Kurdish aspirations as a hostile plot to partition Turkey.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country, two systems conflicts with the unitary-state emphasis of the National State Declaration.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine descent of rulers contradicts the secular Republic and Kemalist revolution.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A left-labelled movement would favour progressive taxation over a flat rate; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Kemalist and leftist tradition emphasises education and environment over innate nature; inferred, not documented.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler unbound by law contradicts republican constitutionalism; adherents condemn AKP overreach.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration as a civilisational goal is not addressed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed government is not discussed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Atatürk veneration is intrinsic to Kemalism; applied to national leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court practice is not documented as an ulusalcı issue.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Maoist theory of continuing class struggle is not documented for the present movement, which emphasises national unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not part of the opened declarations.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not state a position on refugee return rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims on territory because co-nationals live there are not documented; the proposed bloc includes the TRNC but is not framed as a claim.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy contradicts the movement's secularism and Kemalist freedom of conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposed to Islamist direction and Kemalist secularism.

common-currency.rationale: Rejecting Western integration and globalist influence implies preferring a national currency; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The bloc includes Azerbaijan, but no pan-Turkist platform is documented.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Homogeneous nation excludes autonomy for minorities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The statement concerns minority strategy and is not addressed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not documented as a doctrine of the current movement despite Perinçek's Maoist origins.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The sources do not address judicial review; adherents criticise AKP but also support Kemalist guardian institutions, so split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not documented as an ulusalcı issue.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Production-first independence; full autarky not stated.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The movement opposes world-economy integration and does not discuss trade-agreement standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral over material incentives is a Maoist idea, but no source documents it for the present movement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco-style insurgency is not documented; the Vatan Party works through electoral politics.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Kemalist republic abolished imperial titles, and the movement defends that revolution; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Opposes Western hegemony and imperial interference.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism sustaining the nation-state; inferred emphasis.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a US debate not covered in sources; there is no basis to lean.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money-creation reform is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources show no view on capitalism's crisis tendencies, though they describe Western civilisation as in crisis.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Eurasian bloc includes ex-Ottoman Syria and Iraq; unresolved.

delink-world-market.rationale: The party wants a production revolution and reduced dependence on the world economy but not a full break; unresolved.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Maoist theory is not documented for the present movement, so neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Private freedom to discriminate conflicts with a state-centred outlook that stresses national unity and secular citizenship.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The sources do not address constitutional entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Adherents defend the Lausanne settlement as part of Kemalist founding, but sources do not state views on colonial treaties.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Kemalist tradition vests sovereignty in the national assembly; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not mentioned in any opened source.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not mentioned in any opened source.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Withdrawal contradicts a mobilising movement that urges citizens to organise in the Vatan Party.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory is not documented for the movement.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not documented for the movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-imperialism and Third Worldism are keywords.

native-born-offices.rationale: A homogeneity-minded movement that objects to migration would likely reserve offices for natives; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: National roads to socialism fit a nationalist left that rejects foreign direction; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Production revolution aims at domestic production.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Kemalists accepted the Lausanne borders, though some invoke the National Pact; the sources do not settle this.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as a constitutional value is not discussed in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Equating fascism and communism is not addressed; the movement has both leftist and nationalist roots.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American historiography does not feature in these sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A nation-centred, heritage-minded movement would likely defend historic monuments; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not discussed in any source.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic-violence policy is not discussed in any source.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Western orientation seen as dysfunctional but left Kemalists remain Westernisers.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is the movement's base and Kemalist guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work pay is not discussed in any source.

filial-duty.rationale: Socially conservative outlooks usually stress duty to parents, though no source documents it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service examination is not discussed, though Kemalist bureaucracy is merit-based.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The party's production-and-independence line suggests blocking foreign control of strategic industry; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in the sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are not documented; the movement works through standard party politics.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatised pensions conflict with the left label and state-centred economics; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land tenure is not documented for the movement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget approval is not discussed, though adherents oppose executive overreach.

single-official-language.rationale: Wikipedia and the Substack analysis describe the nation as homogeneous and secular, and Turkish as sole language follows Kemalist nationalism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalists and sovereignty-minded movements tend to restrict foreign land ownership; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: US-style disparate-impact doctrine is not discussed in sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism critique is not documented, though the party stresses production over consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Funding foreign insurgents is not documented; adherents accuse the West of doing so against Turkey.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Adherents oppose domination by great powers, so troop intervention against an ally leaving a bloc is rejected; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Left-labelled and anti-globalist adherents likely see corporate lobbying as harmful; not specifically documented.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign plots against Turkey are the movement's core theme, so limiting foreign-funded NGOs and media fits.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nationalists commonly favour population growth, but the sources do not document it; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency limits on property are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: A left-labelled, production-focused movement plausibly supports state employment guarantees, though no source states it; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Skeptical of Western democracy promotion; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A statist, law-and-order nationalism holds that citizens owe obedience to the republic's laws; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Total independence and resistance to Western domination imply that no state may intervene in another's internal affairs, as the Turkey Analyst piece describes.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in any opened source.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Wikipedia reports ulusalcı conspiracy theories that name Greeks, Arabs and Armenians among plotters.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Socially conservative adherents would defend marriage as a legal institution; inferred from Wikipedia's note on social conservatism.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not discussed in any opened source.

local-production.rationale: The party's slogan of a production revolution implies favouring domestic production, though not necessarily hyper-local; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement organises through formal parties such as the Vatan Party, the opposite of small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty and independence from Western institutions imply national constitutions outrank international courts; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined as secular and ethnically homogeneous per the Substack analysis, not by shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ritual submission to a leading power contradicts the slogan of a totally independent Turkey.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal retention weakens the unitary state the declaration stresses; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal property under common ownership of means of production is a Marxist formula not documented for this nationalist movement.

defeat-communism.rationale: Self-described left nationalists with Maoist roots would not call for defeating communism; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The party plans to convert private schools into public ones, opposing a mixed provider model.

religion-illusion.rationale: Kemalists defend secularism but not atheism or the Marxist view of religion as consolation, so the answer is neutral.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The sources do not record whether adherents credit capitalism with progress; Marxist and nationalist traditions diverge.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality is not discussed beyond a note on social conservatism, so there is no basis to lean.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is not documented for the movement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Kemalist language reform removed Arabic and Persian words, and nationalists continue such purism; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with minority nations contradict the unitary-state emphasis, so inclined to reject them; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small cooperative communes conflict with a centralised nation-state and production programme.

majority-settlement.rationale: Encouraging majority settlement in minority regions is not documented in the sources.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Whether adherents claim a third way is not confirmed in opened sources; the movement blends left and nationalist elements.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Radicalised Kemalist historiography is used to prove historic Turkish ties, which supports stronger historical claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No opened source reports Holocaust denial in the movement, so rejection is assumed by default.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Opposes promotion of homosexuality, not criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Adherents are themselves in the opposition to AKP and would not endorse suppressing opposition; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A secularist movement opposes civil punishment of blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism and Third Worldism are keywords of the movement, rejecting colonial exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A secularist movement does not frame resistance as a religious obligation; it speaks in national terms.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Declaring rulers illegitimate for not following religious law is an Islamist idea ulusalcılar oppose.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct local participation is not documented; the movement works through party and state institutions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional theory is not documented for the movement, and its nation-over-class stance suggests rejection; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Perinçek rejects what he calls the imposition of a third gender, so legal recognition of gender identity is opposed.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in any opened source.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Adherents identify as left-wing, though critics call it nationalism in leftist clothing; the left label is held, not discarded.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist alienation is not documented as a theme for the present movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement opposes Islamism but its adherents are largely Muslim-born Turks claiming Western orientation; a civilisational incompatibility claim is not documented.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: National sovereignty and secularism contradict the idea that authority comes from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secularism and the Kemalist tradition imply a ban on religious dress for officials and state-school pupils, though no source quotes the rule.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment-law issues like nondisclosure agreements are not discussed in any opened source.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme combines state-led production with rent rules but does not name a social-market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The army is the movement's base, and the party wants a national military-industrial complex.

rich-first.rationale: Staged development is not discussed; the programme stresses production for all.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: A totally independent Turkey implies avoiding bloc subordination, though adherents also seek closer ties with Russia and China.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession contradicts the republicanism of the Kemalist revolution the party champions.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialism and criticism of world-economy integration suggest rejecting IMF conditions; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Republican Kemalist equal citizenship rejects a property franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not documented for the movement.

reification.rationale: Lukácsian reification is not documented for the movement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources do not cover press ownership critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Republican legalism and criticism of AKP personal rule suggest support for standing laws; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: A homogeneous-nation view is ethnic, but a racial franchise contradicts republican citizenship; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is not discussed in any opened source.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not discussed in any opened source.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A secularist movement opposes legal religious marriage barriers; inferred from secularism.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Conspiracy theories name minorities, but no source documents shop boycotts and secularism opposes religious discrimination; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Kemalist reform of religion versus adherents' disinterest in doctrine; no documented view.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: A left label and production focus suggest concern about concentrated wealth; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Given rejection of promoting homosexuality and army ties, open service is likely opposed; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Kemalist secularism is state neutrality or control of religion, not atheist promotion; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A security-focused state-centred movement opposes abolition of policing.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Communal power-sharing contradicts the unitary national state of the declaration.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: A left-labelled statist movement would prefer state to charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy conflicts with traditional party politics; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office is outside the movement's concerns.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Kemalist civil code equality between spouses is a republican legacy; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Objection to migration and nation-first stance imply opposition; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Perinçek's election declaration proposes freezing rents for three years, ceilings on new contracts and monitoring boards.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not documented; state-led production favours owning technology.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Atatürk-era youth organisation tradition exists, but sources do not state a position.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Opposition to US domination suggests opposing foreign nuclear weapons on Turkish soil; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The programme seeks an end to US domination and questions NATO membership, implying objection to foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Armenia is named among the alleged plotters, and ulusalcı historiography contests genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Left label suggests income should reward work; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism is contrary to the army-centred movement.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Radicalised Kemalist historiography traces Turkish identity continuously from ancient origins; inferred from that.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Perinçek's rejection of the third gender implies rejection of constructivism about sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Post-structuralist feminism contradicts the movement's rejection of gender-identity politics; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring those who die for the nation (şehit) is central to Turkish army-aligned nationalism; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement's rationalist, secular outlook rejects spiritual framings of politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Gathering diaspora versus cultural centre is not documented; the movement emphasises the territorial state.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement prioritises state security and revolution over cultural renewal first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological gender language is not discussed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: A homogeneity-minded view of the nation suggests economic control by the majority; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging regions for one people contradicts the unitary state, notably regarding Kurdish areas.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement's socialist content versus nationalism is unresolved in the sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The programme favours state provision and public control; inferred for water and local transport.

second-chamber.rationale: Turkey's Kemalist parliament is unicameral and no source calls for a second chamber; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production contradicts the centralised national state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal delegates without governing power contradicts the unitary state.

family-wage.rationale: Left-leaning and socially conservative adherents plausibly support family wages; inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A security-minded state would resist untraceable payments; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: A security-minded state would resist online anonymity; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: State and nation primacy contradicts a person-over-state principle; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement's emphasis on enlightenment and secularism makes a politics serving spiritual nature unlikely; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Revocable regional powers match the unitary state the party insists on.

gm-crops.rationale: Food sovereignty and national production concerns suggest distrust of foreign agribusiness; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is touched only by Perinçek's Istanbul plan, so no clear view.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Racial group organising conflicts with a single-nation outlook; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Ethnic pride may be compatible with Turkish nationalism, but racial framing is not documented.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Kemalist defence rhetoric versus the Blue Homeland doctrine; unresolved.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A worldwide conspiracy against Turkey, including plans to partition it through the Kurds, is the central theme attributed to ulusalcilar.

missingStatements.text: Foreign powers are plotting to partition and weaken my country.
missingStatements.rationale: A world-wide conspiracy against Turkey by the US, EU states, Greece, Israel and Armenia is the central theme attributed to ulusalcılar, and the Vatan Party sees hostile forces using Kurds to partition Turkey.

notes: The strand is partly a conspiracy-oriented current, and the sources are mostly secondary or press reports of party declarations; economic and social-policy answers are inferred. Wikipedia's article is a stub, and left-wing adherents dispute whether the label is compatible with leftism.
